- Overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp upward spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast periods; adjust upward by 3–7% if recent history shows sustained upward trend.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term volatility; dampen forecast momentum after 3–5 consecutive days of high volatility.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless confirmed by macro indicators.
- Lagged response: if true outcome is >5% above forecast at day 10+, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid forecasting spikes in price after 30-day high; cap forecast at 10% below recent 30-day high unless confirmed by policy or supply shocks.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >15% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 5–10% to avoid runaway overestimation.
